$comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for resistance calculation. See docs/adr/0004-domain-model-and-resistance.md
Model: resistance = (bodyweight + vestLb) * bodyFraction + barLb + boardWeightLb,
all multiplied by sin(angleDeg), then by pulleyFactor (0.5 for cable exercises).
angleDeg values are the incline angle at each rail notch, level 1 (shallowest) first.
boardWeightLb is the effective mass of the glideboard assembly riding the incline. It was
DERIVED, not published: regressing each row of Total Gym's published resistance charts
against bodyweight yields slope == sin(angleDeg) and a constant non-zero intercept;
intercept / sin(angleDeg) is stable across all levels of a given profile and equals the
board mass. Accuracy is +/- ~1 lb because the published charts round to whole pounds.
Both implementations (C# TotalGymLogBook.Domain and client/src/resistance.ts) must read
this file. Parity is enforced by tests/ against data/resistance-expected.json.

notes: DO NOT trust the published 10-level angle column. It reads 5.2, 10.6, 12.5, 14.3, 16.2,
18.0, 19.9, 21.8, 23.8, 25.8 -- which is the 12-level angle list with two entries deleted,
and it does not reproduce the chart's own resistance numbers. Level 5 is printed as 16.2
deg (sin 0.279) but its resistance row regresses to a slope of 0.240 (13.9 deg).
First and last levels match; the middle is misaligned, consistent with an editing error
The angleDeg values here are back-solved from the chart's resistance columns via
asin(slope), which yields a smooth, physically plausible progression.
Needs confirmation by tape measure on a real 10-level machine before shipping.
